title: Ordinal powers: exponentiation and Cantor normal form
summary: Infinite powers describe ordered blocks and give every ordinal a unique finite normal form.
abstract: Countably many copies of the natural-number order, placed one after another, form a longer well-order that is still countable. Repeating this construction leads to ordinal powers, which describe order rather than count functions. Cantor normal form says that every nonzero ordinal has a unique finite expression as a sum of decreasing powers of omega, the first infinite ordinal, with positive integer coefficients. This gives a systematic way to compare ordinals and understand how adding them changes their order.
